case.case_title: The Public Services United Nurses Union v. Montague Jayewickrema, Minister of Public Administration and Others
case.source_citation: S.C. Application No 4/87, decided on 29 April 1988

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the Cabinet decision discriminated against striking nurses on the basis of political opinion or union affiliation, violating Article 12(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed that the increments were granted primarily to members of a rival union affiliated with the ruling party, thus discriminating on grounds of political opinion and union membership.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied that the decision was discriminatory on prohibited grounds, asserting it was a reward for duty and a legitimate administrative measure.
key_facts: The rival union (7th respondent) was affiliated with the ruling party and had influence with the government.
The increments were granted mainly to members of this rival union and not to the striking nurses or other public officers.
The strike was settled unconditionally without punishment or reward to the striking nurses.
Other public officers who worked during the strike were excluded from the benefit.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court recognized that discrimination on grounds such as political opinion or union affiliation is prohibited under Article 12(2). The arbitrary grant of benefits to a favored group linked to the ruling party, excluding others similarly situated, constituted impermissible discrimination.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The increments were granted primarily to members of a union affiliated with the ruling party, creating an unjustified advantage and discriminating against the petitioners and other public officers who did not share that affiliation.
principles_established: Discrimination on grounds including political opinion or union affiliation violates Article 12(2).
Government decisions must not confer benefits or impose disadvantages based on such prohibited grounds.

outcome.holding: The court held that the Cabinet decision discriminated against the petitioners on prohibited grounds under Article 12(2) and was therefore unconstitutional.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The decision was declared null and void with costs awarded to the petitioners.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was materially engaged because the court found the Cabinet decision discriminated on the basis of political opinion and union affiliation, which are prohibited grounds under this clause.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The benefits of the proposal accrued primarily to officers of a particular union having affiliations with the ruling party, and the decision was arbitrary and discriminatory, violating Article 12 of the Constitution.
